title: The November 2024 House hearing
notes: The 13 November 2024 hearing, where the Immaculate Constellation report was entered.

lead.text: On 13 November 2024 two House Oversight subcommittees, with Nancy Mace presiding, heard sworn witnesses Tim Gallaudet, Luis Elizondo, Michael Shellenberger and Michael Gold, and entered into the record a 12-page document describing an unacknowledged special access programme called Immaculate Constellation.

summary.text: The joint hearing of the Cybersecurity, Information Technology and Government Innovation subcommittee and the National Security, the Border and Foreign Affairs subcommittee was chaired by Mace with Glenn Grothman co-chairing, and printed as Serial No. 118-135.
It is the hearing at which the Immaculate Constellation report entered the congressional record: Shellenberger delivered the document that morning and testified to its contents under oath.

Elizondo, a former Defense Department official, answered yes under oath when asked whether the government has run secret crash retrieval programmes, and said he agreed with Grusch's 2023 testimony, while the same printed record notes that agencies had not substantiated Grusch's claims.

Gallaudet testified to an email about a 2015 Navy safety-of-flight issue that he says vanished from recipients' accounts the next day, and Gold, a member of NASA's UAP study team, testified on stigma and reporting.

record.text: The hearing was held on 13 November 2024 at 11:30 am in 2154 Rayburn. The witness list of record is Rear Admiral Tim Gallaudet (Ret.), chief executive of Ocean STL Consulting; Luis Elizondo, author and former Defense Department official; Michael Shellenberger, founder of Public; and Michael Gold, former NASA associate administrator and member of the NASA UAP Independent Study Team.
Mace opened by saying that certain individuals had not wanted the hearing to happen because they feared what might be disclosed.

Mace entered into the record the 12-page document Shellenberger brought that day, describing its first section as about the unacknowledged special access programme called Immaculate Constellation and its second as about US government imagery intelligence. She announced that Burchett held the document and would enter it.

The Index of Documents lists the Mellon hearing letter and the Immaculate Constellation report submitted by Mace, documents related to UAP submitted by Burchett, and Questions for the Record to all four witnesses submitted by Burlison.

The report is not printed in the GPO hearing volume, which lists it and points to the committee repository. As published there it is twelve scanned pages with no cover letter, author name, classification marking or control number; its first page says the public version was approved for release by the State Department's Bureau of Global Public Affairs, and its introduction says it reached Congress through the UAP whistleblower mechanisms of the FY23 NDAA and the FY23 Intelligence Authorization Act.
The report organises its public version into seven categories of evidence, and its imagery section catalogues nine incidents, each headed by the combatant command it came from.
Mace read Karl Nell's statement that nonhuman intelligence exists into the record from the chair; Nell did not testify.
Gallaudet's statement urged members to use their subpoena power against hostile witnesses and to stop funding UAP efforts hidden from congressional oversight.
Asked by Rep. Boebert whether he knew of an alleged Defense Department programme manipulating human genetics with non-human genetic material, Gold answered no.

claimed.text: Elizondo testified under oath that the government has conducted secret UAP crash retrieval programmes designed to identify and reverse engineer craft of non-human origin. Asked whether he had been read into them, he said that would need a closed session.

Asked by Burchett, Elizondo said he had worked with Grusch at US Space Force and agreed with Grusch's testimony about a multi-decade crash retrieval and reverse-engineering programme. The board records it as the only sworn second-source affirmation of Grusch's central allegation, given by someone who had worked with him.
Elizondo testified that he signed a government document in a SCIF, in the presence of a security officer, that barred him from discussing crash retrieval.

Elizondo testified that an aerospace contractor had asked to divest itself of material collected in the 1950s and that this did not happen; asked about the reported Lockheed Martin and Bigelow Aerospace transfer, he said it was blocked and that a required Secretary of the Air Force memorandum never came.
Asked by Mace whether material goes to particular contractors because of their expertise, Elizondo agreed that different contractors have different levels of expertise.
Elizondo's written testimony alleges that advanced technologies not made by any government are monitoring sensitive military installations, and a multi-decade secretive arms race.

Shellenberger testified that the report describes Immaculate Constellation as a central or parent programme consolidating UAP observations from tasked and untasked collection platforms, with incidents including orbs forcing an F-22 out of its patrol area. The report came to him from an alleged insider: he said he knows the author but would not say whether his sources sit inside the Defense Department, and a source told him the programme is controlled by the White House and run by the Defense Department to avoid Title 10.

Gallaudet testified that in January 2015 the Fleet Forces Command operations officer emailed all subordinate commanders under the subject URGENT SAFETY OF FLIGHT ISSUE with the GO FAST video, that the email vanished from recipients' accounts the next day, and that he concluded it must have been classified within a special access programme managed by an intelligence agency.

Gold testified that stigma prevents scientific inquiry, that Alex Dietrich was mocked by colleagues and her incident went years without investigation, and recommended that NASA work with the FAA on civilian pilot reporting.

contested.text: The same hearing record states that agencies briefed since 2023, including the DoD Inspector General's office, had not substantiated Grusch's claims despite questioning inside and outside the SCIF.

AARO's Historical Record Report Volume I, released eight months earlier, asserts that none of AARO's interviewees had firsthand knowledge and that the alleged programmes do not exist or were disestablished. The board infers that its finding of no NDAs containing UAP information cannot be squared with Elizondo's sworn account of a SCIF document.

The Department says it has no record of a programme called Immaculate Constellation, and former AARO director Sean Kirkpatrick has denied its existence. On the board's reading a no-record answer is a records assertion rather than a denial that the programme exists, and no AARO product has addressed the name.

The Index of Documents calls it a Pentagon report and Mace called it the original document from the Pentagon, but the published pages carry no author, classification marking or control number, and their first page credits the State Department with approving the public version.

Asked whether he had been read into Immaculate Constellation, Elizondo said he was not authorised to confirm or deny any special access programme by name or trigraph, which confirms nothing either way.

In 2025 a separate self-identified whistleblower said he found the programme in a folder labelled 2018 Schriever Wargame, and Jason Colavito concluded he had mistaken fictitious wargame documents for real ones. The board notes this addresses the 2025 claim, not the 2024 document.

The Department's position since 2019 is that Elizondo had no assigned responsibilities for AATIP and did not lead it, and Kirkpatrick has attributed the crash-retrieval narrative to AATIP and Robert Bigelow's circle.

questions: Who wrote the twelve-page report, and did it originate in the Pentagon as the Index of Documents describes it?
Has the Department or AARO ever answered the report in writing, beyond a no-record statement to the press?
What was the document Elizondo says he signed in a SCIF, and who holds it?
Who sent the January 2015 Fleet Forces Command email, and why, and on whose authority, did it vanish from recipients' accounts?
Who holds the material Elizondo says was blocked from transfer, the question he would answer only in closed session?
When and in what capacity did Elizondo and Grusch work together at US Space Force, and does that bear on how independent his affirmation is?
